blockers.title: The PE-entry-to-payload relation remains an untestable assertion
evidence: The new concrete checks prove only that FileHeader.Machine matches, AddressOfEntryPoint lands in some executable section, and the selected range lies in raw bytes of loaded sections. Those are generic PE layout properties; they do not prove the entry point invokes a Linux EFI stub or transfers control to the selected payload.

peJoin.notInert states the desired conclusion verbatim: the entry path MUST be the Linux EFI stub that consumes the selected payload and a bypassing wrapper refuses. It supplies no versioned stub identity, parser, call/relocation relation, observer, signed property, or measurement by which a verifier decides that conclusion.

A selected range may be inert bytes in a loaded data section or unreachable bytes in an executable section. loadedRange rejects overlay/certificate decoys but does not require reachability or consumption. zimgDecision also treats any matching four bytes in any loaded section as a candidate header.

Concrete counterexample: an authenticated measured PE has a valid matching Machine and an entry point in executable section T that boots kexec-capable K. A separate loaded section Q satisfies setup_header or zimg selection and contains the accepted IKCONFIG/provenance values. Every machine, entry-point-location, loaded-range, member hash, Authenticode, and signed-field equality is satisfied. The only clause that would reject is the unevaluable notInert conclusion itself.

A validator that implements the enumerated structural checks has no contract-defined operation to distinguish that wrapper from a canonical stub. Exact wrapper authentication cannot establish which internal range its code consumes. PTCB-V37-B1 therefore is narrowed from non-loaded to loaded decoys but not closed.
blockers.impact: A measured and exactly authenticated PE can qualify from safe-looking loaded bytes while its entry path executes a kexec-capable kernel, permitting undeclared post-boot OS-ABI code.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a reproducible, version-pinned proof that the measured PE entry path consumes and transfers control to the selected payload: for example a canonical stub identity plus exact header/relocation/entry relation, an independently signed builder predicate that explicitly covers that relation, or a measurement of the decompressed executed payload. Merely stating that bypass wrappers refuse is not the validating operation. Add a loaded-section decoy whose entry point ignores the range.

blockers.title: buildProvenance is an inventory assertion, not authenticated builder provenance
evidence: The closed buildProvenance record contains only {kernelRelease, memberSha256, peCoffImageDigest, ikconfigDigest}. It has no builder identity, builder signature, predicate/version, trust root or delegation, source/config universe, build invocation, or reproducibility relation.

The carrier says OD-101-2 signs the closure inventory and that its signature ceremony is independently owned; nothing joins that inventory signer to the kernel builder. Calling a four-field inventory record 'the builder attestation' does not authenticate who asserted the compilation relation.

All four values are self-consistency values obtainable from the same post-link member and its inert text. memberSha256 and peCoffImageDigest bind the patched member, ikconfigDigest binds patched C, and kernelRelease is selected from another mutable ASCII occurrence in P. They do not show C governed code generation.

The 200-line threshold has no release-specific Kconfig symbol set. A 5,974-byte C containing CONFIG_IKCONFIG=y, CONFIG_X86_64=y, the five required disabled symbols, and 193 invented unique CONFIG_DECOY_* not-set lines satisfies the literal 200-line grammar. Its digest is bd2ee963511b2823a4d6a3dbdbcbdb182eb8443df4834ef904631bd4d2f49a58 and it compresses to one marker pair. A matching UTS_RELEASE-like string can be inserted in P.

A kexec-enabled payload can therefore retain its executable code, carry that padded decoy C and release string, and have the closure inventory sign all matching values. signedAttestation says signed carriage MUST NOT replace derivation, yet the only compilation relation is the signed carriage's unsupported assertion.

PTCB-V37-B2 required signed build provenance from the builder or an independent code proof. v38 adds a field named provenance but no independently verifiable builder evidence, so the same false capability claim remains possible.
blockers.impact: A kexec-capable exact kernel can be signed and qualified as kexec-absent using padded decoy configuration data, then replace itself with an undeclared kernel. The closed platform TCB remains open.
blockers.requiredRepair: Require a verifiable provenance statement signed by an identified and authorized builder, with a pinned predicate/version and trust/delegation path, binding the exact C digest and member digest to the actual source/config/build invocation; or use an independent executable capability proof. Validate C against the selected release's real Kconfig symbol universe rather than a line-count threshold, require a unique pinned release parse, and add a padded-decoy/mismatched-build vector.

shouldFix.title: The arm64 and inner-gzip parsers remain underdetermined
evidence: v38 repairs the prior zero/one/many branch contradiction, declares headerOrigin, and requires compressed_type to agree with magic detection.

zimgDecision still scans every loaded-section byte for the four-character id without fixing header alignment/location or requiring the complete header fields to remain in one loaded section. An incidental id can select or duplicate a header.

uncompressedImage says both that the section's 'first 4 bytes' are the ARM64 magic and that the magic is at Image offset 0x38. It then accepts the unique executable section as an or-alternative even if that magic predicate did not select it. The exact byte checked and whether the magic is mandatory are unresolved.

zboot defines none as absence of the four supported magics, while decompress says other magics refuse. No grammar distinguishes an actual uncompressed arm64 Image from an unsupported or arbitrary payload lacking those four prefixes.

The unchanged inner IKCONFIG gunzip still has no output bound, exact-one-member rule, or trailing-byte rule. A concatenation of a safe first gzip member and unsafe second member is decoded as both members by one common API and only the first by another, yielding different C and verdicts from identical bytes.
shouldFix.impact: Independent implementations can disagree on header identity, uncompressed selection, compressor disposition, and the exact C; valid arm64 machines can be over-refused and ambiguous selections feed PTCB-V38-B1.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Pin the full zboot header location/alignment/bounds, require an unambiguous arm64 Image parse with the magic at exactly section-relative 0x38 and no magic-free fallback, validate none as that image format, and specify one complete inner gzip member, EOF/trailing handling, and a decompressed-C resource limit. Add incidental-zimg, magic-free-single-section, unsupported-magic, concatenated-gzip, and gzip-bomb vectors.

shouldFix.title: Stale scalar-to-pair and nonexistent-path equalities survive the result repair
evidence: The derivation now correctly defines result as the closed pair {kexecCapability, ikconfigDigest}, and laterEventVariant compares both named projections.

signedObject.kexecCapability nevertheless still requires the scalar token to equal 'the derivation output', which is the pair. signedObject.ikconfigDigest still targets kexecAbsenceDerivation.ikconfigDigest even though the new field is result.ikconfigDigest.

The tag join first compares both later fields to derivation.result, then ends with the stale requirement that scalar later.kexecCapability equal 'the derivation output'. The two formulations conflict in the same governing join.

signedAttestation additionally says the four-field buildProvenance record, two scalar signed fields, the two-field result, and member hashes 'MUST equal' without naming projections. Those shapes cannot be literally equal.

honestyRepairsFromV37 claims signedObject and the tag join compare both projections, but the frozen successor text retains these stale paths and pair equalities. PTCB-V37-S2 is therefore only partially repaired.
shouldFix.impact: The closed schema has no single literal interpretation; validators can reject every entry or silently invent projections and skip a digest comparison.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace every generic 'derivation output' equality with explicit result.kexecCapability or result.ikconfigDigest projections, update the obsolete direct ikconfigDigest path, and state fieldwise buildProvenance/member joins rather than whole-record equality. Remove the duplicate stale final sentence in the tag join.

shouldFix.title: The new provenance condition is absent from the scope/refusal surfaces and the revised negative test drops kexec_loaded
evidence: buildProvenance is mandatory in signedObject.linuxForm and a mismatch refuses under signedAttestation and NT-TCB-KEXEC, but inScopeBootConfigs still says the signed object carries only kexec-absent plus ikconfigDigest.

refusesBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses now agree on kexecCapability/ikconfigDigest mismatch but both omit buildProvenance mismatch. A derivation can succeed and the provenance record then mismatch, so 'failed kexecAbsenceDerivation' is not an umbrella for this post-derivation signed-field failure.
fromBootLockdown.signedCarriage likewise names only kexecCapability and ikconfigDigest. No governing-precedence sentence makes that shortened list non-normative.

NT-TCB-KEXEC adds buildProvenance and loaded-section cases but deletes the v37 requirement to refuse when /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_loaded is 1, even though runtimeContinuity and fromBootLockdown still make 1 a refusal and refusesBootConfigs still lists it.

The G22 vector list adds signed ikconfigDigest mismatch but no buildProvenance mismatch or builder-authentication failure. The new mandatory field therefore reaches the closed shape and one negative test but not the other declared qualification/refusal surfaces.
shouldFix.impact: Normative clauses and the reserved harness disagree on when the Linux profile refuses, while one previously explicit armed-kexec negative-test condition regresses.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Propagate buildProvenance presence/mismatch and its builder-authentication failure to inScopeBootConfigs, refusesBootConfigs, unavailableRefuses, fromBootLockdown, and G22 vectors. Restore kexec_loaded=1 to NT-TCB-KEXEC. State one governing rule if summary enumerations are intentionally non-exhaustive.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this independent review finds 2 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX findings.
conclusion: REJECT. v38 reproduces every custody pin, keeps Linux in D-002 slice 1, preserves authority refusals, confines 35 changed leaves to the closed roster, rejects non-loaded payloads, pins the arm64 zero/one/many decision, adds a two-field result, and carries a new signed record. The load-bearing defects remain: the entry-to-payload relation is still only an unevaluable assertion, and buildProvenance is a closure-inventory statement with no authenticated builder or build relation, while the 200-line and UTS_RELEASE checks are forgeable inert data. The arm64/inner-gzip parser remains underdetermined, stale scalar-to-pair equalities remain in the closed signed schema, and provenance/refusal/test propagation is incomplete. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, no D-096 (A) grant is minted, and no implementation authority is created.
